name: Fleece-Hollow
geological_features: Fractured ice plains with deep crevasses
specific_features: Surface frost with a soft, fleece-like texture due to unique crystallization
Deep cavern system with acoustically resonant chambers
description: Fleece-Hollow is a small, frigid world whose surface is coated in a peculiar form of frost that grows in soft, fibrous crystals rather than the typical angular structures found on most ice bodies. This frost, up to half a meter thick in places, gives the entire planet a soft, muffled appearance, as though it has been draped in white fleece. Beneath this gentle exterior lies a fractured ice crust riddled with crevasses and cave systems that extend deep into the planet's frozen interior.

The thin atmosphere barely registers on instruments, composed primarily of trace nitrogen and noble gases that cling to the surface through the planet's weak gravity. Sound travels poorly in the open, but within the cave systems, acoustic properties change dramatically. Certain chambers amplify even faint vibrations into resonant booms that can be felt through suit boots, the planet's frozen bones humming with stored energy from tidal flexing and ancient geological processes.

The cave systems of Fleece-Hollow are its primary point of scientific interest. They extend far deeper than models predicted, reaching down hundreds of kilometers through layered ice of varying composition. The deepest explored chambers contain methane ice formations of extraordinary delicacy, grown in near-zero gravity conditions over millions of years into fractal structures that shatter at a touch. Robotic surveyors have mapped only a fraction of the total network, with sonar returns suggesting vast unexplored volumes below current penetration depth.

A proposal to use Fleece-Hollow as a methane ice mining site was shelved after structural analysis showed the cave systems make the crust dangerously unstable for heavy equipment. The planet's real value may be as a natural laboratory for studying ice crystal formation under exotic conditions, with potential applications in materials science and cryogenic engineering. The fleece-like surface frost, in particular, has properties that no one has been able to replicate synthetically, suggesting it forms through processes not yet understood. Fleece-Hollow keeps its softest secrets close.
